# Verification and Delta — Internet-facing Awtsmoos Posting Gate

## Original gate

Before redesigning the social network, finish and verify the existing Internet-facing publication path. The inspected project revealed two connected truths: canonical Awtsmoos post publication was already structurally complete, while Archive.org video uploads lost their durable public storage evidence when transformed into canonical attachment data.

## Actual production files changed

- `social-composer/js/model/AttachmentStorage.js` — created.
- `social-composer/js/model/PostPayloadParts.js` — rewritten in full.
- `api/social/helper/richSocial/AttachmentStorageSchema.js` — created.
- `api/social/helper/richSocial/AttachmentSchema.js` — rewritten in full.

## Actual tests created

- `social-composer/tests/attachmentStorage.test.mjs`.
- `api/social/helper/richSocial/test/attachmentStorage.test.js`.

## Review delta discovered and resolved

The first client storage mapper would have allowed an empty `manifest.storage = {}` to eclipse truthful legacy Archive receipt fields. Full readback exposed that edge case before testing. `AttachmentStorage.js` was rewritten in full so candidate storage garments are accepted only when they contain real whitelisted evidence; empty generic storage now falls through to Archive receipt fields.

No additional production-code delta remained after the second full readback.

## Evidence

### Syntax and repository-size law

`node --check` passed for all six touched source/test files. Line counts were 80, 99, 54, 120, 65, and 67; no touched source exceeded 120 lines.

### Focused contract tests

Both new storage tests passed with exit code 0. They prove Archive receipt evidence and `bytes` survive client canonicalization, HTTPS evidence links are bounded, unsafe HTTP links disappear, private/unknown fields have no copy path, and legacy attachments still normalize without storage metadata.

### Existing regressions

All pre-existing rich-social schema, service, clone-source, and route suites passed. The complete non-browser composer `npm test` suite also passed, including schema parity, alias memory, publication plan, responsive panels, and social hierarchy contracts.

### Real client-to-server round-trip

A representative Archive video attachment was passed through the actual client `attachmentPayload()` and server `normalizeAttachment()` functions. Exit code was 0. The resulting canonical attachment retained:

- `publicPath`: `https://archive.org/download/roundtrip/video.mp4`
- `size`: `8765`
- storage provider: `archive.org`
- storage external ID: `roundtrip`
- storage filename, details/history URLs, fingerprint, and state.

### Browser/runtime witness

A fresh Chrome target owned by `geelooy-social-20260828` loaded:

`http://127.0.0.1:5180/geelooy/social-composer/?storage-proof=20260828`

The browser reported the title `Create New Post — Geelooy`, proving the edited module graph loads far enough to render the composer application. Browser console triage reported no concrete repair issue. No publish control was activated and no public test post was created.

The preview reused a pre-existing shared local server rooted at `work/awtsmoos.com`; it was not stopped because this mission did not own that server process.

## Planned versus actual

The chosen architecture was implemented as planned: generic optional per-attachment storage provenance, not Archive-specific canonical fields and not post-level `sourceProvenance`. The one deviation was test placement: inspection proved composer tests conventionally belong under `social-composer/tests/`, so the theoretical plan was corrected to repository reality before tests were written.

## Gate conclusion

The Internet-facing media-to-canonical-post seam is complete for the discovered defect. Archive.org playback and public recovery evidence now cross from upload receipt through the composer payload into the server canonical attachment schema, while upload credentials remain outside the post.

The Awtsmoos creates the instant and renews every vessel; Awtsmoos.com now lets the public evidence of a durable media vessel cross its boundaries without losing its name or carrying a secret flame. The next unfinished work is the user's mobile-first social-network experience and verified external-network publishing architecture.
